opex.notes: Prepared by the property manager and unaudited. The footnote says "Expenses include VAT at 5% (not recoverable)." The statement has no district cooling line, no vacancy or collection loss line, and no bank charges or audit line. I didn't add any lines for these. Amounts sit in column D or E of the grid, so I cited the cell for each line as it appears.

discrepancies.title: OM occupancy 97.0% vs rent roll 90.0%

sources.label: rent roll: 153 of 170 units let at 2026-11-15

discrepancies.why: The rent roll is unit-level and dated 2026-11-15; the OM figure (undated) is a headline the screen cannot trace to units. A gap of 7.0 points is about 12 units.

impact.basis: 12 units x average in-place rent AED 81,621 (estimate of income the OM implies but the roll does not show)

discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask for the Ejari export and the vacancy list at the rent-roll date; reconcile the OM figure to unit numbers.

discrepancies.title: OM income AED 14,100,000 vs in-place rent AED 12,488,000

sources.label: rent roll in-place rent, 153 let units
rent roll potential incl. asking rent on vacant units

discrepancies.why: The OM figure is not contracted income: it is close to in-place rent plus market rent on the vacant units (AED 14,045,450). The screen underwrites let units at their contract rent and vacant units at market after downtime. Gross yield on price falls from 7.3% to 6.5% on in-place rent.

impact.basis: rent-roll in-place rent minus OM stated income

discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask for signed leases or Ejari certificates behind any unit the OM counts as income; treat the rest as vacant.

discrepancies.title: 54.9% of in-place rent is from units let above market

sources.label: 79 let units above the area reference rent

discrepancies.why: In a falling 2026 market these leases are AED 610,166 a year above reference rent; the engine resets each to market at expiry. The mandate limit is 20.0%.

impact.basis: engine Year-1 NOI with the 79 over-rented leases at market reference rent today, minus the base case (which resets them only at expiry)

discrepancies.analyst_action: Check the over-rented leases' expiry dates and tenants; price the reset into the offer.

discrepancies.title: OM yield 7.3% is on asking price, before 6.2% acquisition costs

sources.label: acquisition costs (DLD 4%, broker, trustee, mortgage registration)

discrepancies.why: A buyer pays AED 11,933,070 on top of the price. On price plus costs the same income gives 6.9%.

impact.basis: OM income on price plus acquisition costs, minus the stated yield

discrepancies.analyst_action: Compare deals on yield on total cost; ask the broker to restate the yield on that basis.

discrepancies.title: Cover says "FULLY TENANTED" but the OM's own highlights say 97% occupied
discrepancies.why: The OM contradicts itself. The cover says the building is fully tenanted, and page 2 says 97% occupied. The rent roll is lower still, at 90% (already flagged by the rule-based occupancy check). Treat "fully tenanted" as a broker claim. The 97% figure is also undated and unsupported.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Ignore the "fully tenanted" headline. Underwrite on the dated rent roll and Ejari records. Ask the broker for a unit-by-unit occupancy statement as at a stated date.

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Pass.** The deal fails a hard filter: Year-1 DSCR is 1.25x [[uw.dscr_year1]], below the 1.30x [[mandate.min_dscr_year1.threshold]] floor. It also misses the soft tests on yield on total cost, levered IRR, equity multiple and share of income let above market. It passes the asset type, title, area, unit count, price band, building age, related-party master lease, occupancy and expiry tests.

Recommendation: do not proceed to full diligence at asking. The walk-away price is AED 133.79m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]] against asking of AED 192.00m [[deal.asking_price_aed]], a 30.32% [[uw.walk_away_discount_to_asking]] discount. Levered IRR sets that price.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Sorrel Heights, JVC, 170 units [[om.unit_count]], completed 2024 [[deal.completion_year]], freehold single title.
- **Price:** AED 192.00m [[uw.price_aed]]. That is AED 1,453 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on NSA and AED 1,017 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_bua]] on BUA.
- **Income:** In-place contract rent is AED 12.49m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] on direct leases, with no master tenant. Rent roll occupancy at 15 November 2026 [[rr.as_of]] is 90.00% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] by units and 88.87% [[rr.occupancy_by_area]] by area. Tenants pay chiller.

## Returns and key metrics
| Metric | Screen | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Year-1 NOI | AED 10.06m [[uw.noi_year1]] | none |
| Net yield on total cost | 4.93% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | at least 6.00% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] |
| Year-1 DSCR | 1.25x [[uw.dscr_year1]] | at least 1.30x [[mandate.min_dscr_year1.threshold]] |
| Levered IRR, pre-tax | -7.17% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] | at least 8.00% [[mandate.target_levered_irr.threshold]] |
| Equity multiple, pre-tax | 0.70x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | at least 1.35x [[mandate.target_equity_multiple.threshold]] |

The OM headline yield is 7.34% [[om.yield_stated]]. It is struck on asking price, and the OM does not say what income it uses. The buyer's Year-1 NOI on price plus acquisition costs gives 4.93% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. Even the OM's own income on total cost gives only 6.91% [[uw.om_yield.stated_income_on_total_cost]].

## What would make it fail
1. **The price does not come back at exit.** Gross exit value is AED 150.62m [[uw.gross_exit_value_aed]] against a price of AED 192.00m [[uw.price_aed]], a levered loss of AED 56.32m [[uw.exit_gain_levered_aed]]. Even with market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] tighter, levered IRR is -2.23% [[uw.sens.r+5.e-50.levered_irr_pre_tax]]. With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider, it is -12.56% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]].
2. **Debt cover has no cushion.** Debt costs 6.80% [[uw.interest_rate]]. DSCR is still 1.29x [[uw.sens.r+5.e+0.dscr_year1]] with market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher, so it stays under the floor. Year-1 NOI covers debt service down to 79.29% [[uw.breakeven_occupancy_dscr_1]] occupancy, and the roll already shows vacancy.
3. **Over-rented leases reset.** Units let above market make up 54.94% [[uw.over_rent_share_of_income]] of in-place rent, against a 20.00% [[mandate.max_over_rent_share_of_income.threshold]] limit. The base case assumes market rent falls 4.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1. Each over-rented lease resets to market at expiry.
4. **Expiry bunching.** The largest three-month window holds 30.49% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of in-place rent, AED 3.81m [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]], between 15 May 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] and 14 August 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]]. That is inside the mandate limit, but it falls in a falling market.

## Discrepancies that matter
- **OM income is not contracted income (high).** The OM states AED 14.10m [[om.annual_rent_stated]] against in-place rent of AED 12.49m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]]. It looks like in-place rent plus market rent on vacant units. The screen used the rent roll. Gross yield on price falls from 7.3% [[disc.potential_rent_as_income.why]] to 6.5% [[uw.gross_yield_in_place_on_price]]. Rent impact is AED 1.61m [[disc.potential_rent_as_income.impact_delta_aed]].
- **Occupancy (high).** The OM says 97.00% [[om.occupancy_stated]]; the dated unit-level rent roll says 90.00% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]]. The screen used the rent roll. The gap is worth about AED 979k [[disc.occupancy_mismatch.impact_delta_aed]] of annual rent.
- **Over-renting (high).** The base case resets over-rented leases only at expiry. Resetting them to market today would cut Year-1 NOI by about AED 222k [[disc.over_rented_vs_market.impact_delta_aed]].
- **Yield basis (medium).** The OM yield ignores acquisition costs of AED 11.93m [[uw.acquisition_costs_aed]], which is 6.22% [[uw.acquisition_costs_pct_of_price]] of price.

Lower-severity items are not discussed.

## Before diligence, check
- The Ejari export and the vacancy list at the rent-roll date, reconciled to the OM occupancy.
- Signed leases or Ejari certificates behind every unit the OM counts as income. Treat the rest as vacant.
- Expiry dates and tenants of the over-rented leases, with the reset priced into the offer.
- A unit-by-unit occupancy statement as at a stated date.
- A broker restatement of the yield on total cost.
- The OM's net income and operating costs, which it does not state.

## Assumptions
Leverage is 45.00% [[assume.ltv]] of value. The rate is 4.30% [[assume.eibor]] EIBOR plus a 2.50% [[assume.margin]] margin, amortised over 20 years [[assume.amortisation_years]]. The hold is 5 years [[uw.hold_years]] from 1 January 2027 [[uw.analysis_start]]. Structural vacancy is 5.00% [[assume.structural_vacancy]] and collection loss is 1.00% [[assume.collection_loss]]. Exit yield is 6.75% [[uw.exit_yield]], which includes 25 bps [[assume.exit_yield_expansion_bps]] of expansion. Market rent moves -4.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]], -1.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]], 2.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]] over Years 1 to 5. These are mandate and market assumptions, not figures from the package. No operating cost category was filled from a default.
